![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14194326/assets/4ac748affb35ed10f30febe0c3f6f53e0731646f8611b64731e8fed223b73ed3.png)

A cup of coffee cools over time. The temperature after $x$ minutes, in degrees Fahrenheit, is given by the function $T(x).$ The graph of $T(x)$ is shown above.  

Approximate the rate of change when $x=36$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=11.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=25$ and $x=36.$*

The estimated rate of change when $x=36$ is
{{field-1}} degrees Fahrenheit per minute.
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{T}^{′}(x)≈\frac{T(x)-T(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=36.$  Applying the above formula with $x=36$ and $h=11$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(36) & ≈\frac{T(36)-T(36-11)}{11} \\  & =\frac{T(36)-T(25)}{11} \\  & =\frac{44-45}{11} \\  & =-\frac{1}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $x=36$ is $-\frac{1}{11}$ degrees Fahrenheit per minute.
